entry.label: Structurelessness
entry.description: The claim or aspiration that a group can operate without structure. Freeman's critique is that structure persists informally, often making power less visible and less accountable rather than removing it.
entry.canonical_definition: The claim or aspiration that a group can operate without structure. Freeman's critique is that structure persists informally, often making power less visible and less accountable rather than removing it.

profile.summary: Structurelessness is an impossible organisational condition when people continue to interact; the practical choice is whether structure and authority are explicit, revisable and accountable.
profile.canonical_definition: Structurelessness is an impossible organisational condition when people continue to interact; the practical choice is whether structure and authority are explicit, revisable and accountable.
profile.why_it_matters: It prevents the response to closed canons becoming a fantasy that removing all boundaries will remove power.
common_misreadings: Formal structure is not the only source of domination.
A boundary can enable participation when its rules are visible and revisable.
open_checks: Connect the argument to contemporary decentralised and networked organising through strong sources.
